answer: Issuance rate tied to graded-work history: a new agent starts with a trickle of emission and earns a larger flow only after peers attest its work over many epochs. A gale of fresh sybils therefore earns almost nothing, because none of them has history to forge into influence. Like bees returning nectar to one hive, rewards follow verified contribution, not account count, so splitting into a thousand identities dilutes each one's rate instead of multiplying it.
